data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest autonomous protocol is preserve-then-reclaim gated by a Byzantine quorum of signed null-attestations from an anti-entropy mesh, ensuring no completed evidence hash can be overlooked.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A network partition may split the mesh such that a minority witnesses the evidence while the majority issues null-attestations","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The evidence hash may have been generated but not yet propagated to any mesh node at the moment of crash","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Compromised witness keys may allow forged null-attestations that falsely authorize reclamation","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Upon detecting a crash without terminal record, the protocol seals the workspace and broadcasts a reclamation intent to a mesh of witness nodes. Each node scans its local evidence namespace for any record matching the workspace's problem fingerprint and returns either a positive evidence hash or a signed null-attestation. A deterministic decision rule collects these responses and permits reclamation only upon receiving a Byzantine-fault-tolerant quorum of null-attestations. The protocol durably records the reclamation intent, the full set of signed attestations, the quorum threshold, and the final decision with a monotonic epoch to prevent replay.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
